out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: PIC Duties, Train Employees on Food Safety
violations.observation: Staff was observed not trained in sanitizing procedures, cold holding and hot holding temperatures, and hand washing
violations.corrective_action: The Person in Charge or certified food manager shall train all his/her employees in food safety, including allergy awareness, as it relates to their assigned duties. ALL STAFF NEED TO BE TRAINED IN BASIC FOOD SAFETY PROCEDURES - SANITIZING, FOOD TEMPERATURES, HAND WASHING. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: A certified food manager was not present at the beginning of the inspection
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. A CERTIFIED FOOD MANAGER ARRIVED AT THE END OF THE INSPECTION. A CERTIFIED FOOD MANAGER MUST BE PRESENT AT ALL TIMES OF FOOD PREPARATION. HAVE MULTIPLE STAFF MEMBERS BECOME CERTIFIED FOOD MANAGERS. VISIT THE FAIRFAX COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT CERTIFIED FOOD MANAGER GUIDELINES FOR A FULL LIST OF ACCREDITED ORGANIZATIONS. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: An Employee Health Policy was not presented during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH A COPY OF THE FAIRFAX COUNTY EMPLOYEE ILLNESS AGREEMENT. PIC HAD ALL PRESENT STAFF READ AND SIGN THE AGREEMENT. ALL EMPLOYEES MUST READ AND SIGN A COPY. RETAIN ON SITE FOR FUTURE INSPECTIONS.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: After manipulating the 3 compartment sink faucet and chemical jugs with gloved hands, staff member began mixing sauce with a spatula without washing hands or changing gloves.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS INSTRUCTED STAFF TO TAKE GLOVES OFF AND WASH HANDS BEFORE HANDLING FOOD. STAFF BEGAN WASHING HANDS. SEE WHEN TO WASH HANDOUT.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: 1) Raw ground beef patties was observed being stored above prepared sauces in the walk-in 2) Raw shelled eggs was observed being stored above lettuce
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED STAFF TO MOVE ALL RAW ANIMAL PRODUCTS TO THE RAW MEAT SHELF. EGGS AND BEEF PATTIES WERE PLACED ON THE TOP SHELF ABOVE ALL THE RAW CHICKEN

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) in the 4DWR lowboy cooler: Raw chicken tenders (55f), Raw mixed chicken (55f), Raw chicken wings (51f) 2) in the walk-in cooler: signature sauce containing melted unsalted butter (45f) 3) at ambient at self-service: signature sauce containing melted unsalted butter (74f) Upon discussion with staff, Raw chicken is moved into the 4DWR lowboy cooler from the walk-in cooler every morning. Raw chicken was moved 2 hours prior to inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. STAFF MOVED THE ALL RAW CHICKEN TO THE WALK-IN COOLER TO COOL TO 41f. PIC DISCARDED BOTH SAUCES. NASH & SMASHED (Inspection Date: 07/27/2026) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: PIC presented a food probe thermometer. Thermometer was observed not functioning properly
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. PURCHASE A NEW FOOD PROBE THERMOMETER. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: A box of food was observed being stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PURCHASE DUNNAGE RACK TO ELEVATE ALL FOOD OFF OF THE FLOOR.

violations.title: Food Storage Prohibited under Open Stairwells
violations.observation: Observed a shelf full of bagged ingredients being stored in the hallway outside of the kitchen
violations.corrective_action: Food may not be stored under open stairwells. MOVE ALL FOOD INSIDE THE KITCHEN. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Observed a dirty wet cloth being stored directly on the cutting board
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. STAFF DISCARDED THE WIPING CLOTH. STORE ALL WIPING CLOTHS IN SANITIZER .

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Observed beverage crates being used to elevate fryer oil off the floor
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. PURCHASE DUNNAGE RACKS TO ELEVATE OIL OFF FLOOR AND TO FACILITATE PROPER CLEANING.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: Observed no chlorine test kit on site
violations.corrective_action: PIC ARRIVED WITH CHLORINE TEST KIT.

out_items.name: Toilet facilities properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned

violations.title: Toilet Tissue Supplied
violations.observation: Toilet paper was not observed in the women’s room
violations.corrective_action: Provide toilet tissue at each toilet to minimize hand contact with fecal waste. STAFF REPLACE THE TOILET PAPER.

violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: There is no Certified Food Manager present at the beginning of the inspection. Two staff members present had no certification with them and indicated they were not certified.
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTION : The certified food manager arrived approximately 25 minutes after start of inspection. It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTION: The EHS provided two copies of the Employee Health Policy. Staff read through the policy and signed the document. A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703- 246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTION: Two copies of the vomit diarrhea clean up policy were provided to the CFM. A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. NASH & SMASHED (Inspection Date: 02/09/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding

violations.title: Reheating for Hot Holding, Proper Temp
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: The following food item(s) was not reheated for hot holding to a sufficient temperature and/or time: Facility is using food warmer to reheat cold foods.Macaroni and cheese @103 F and Mashed potatoes @ 120 F were observed reheating in the food warmer.
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTION: Discussed with team that the food warmer cannot be used for reheating and the food was discarded. Time/temperature control for safety food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated to a minimum temperature of 165F for 15 seconds.

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: The certified food manager could not provide a working food temperature measuring device.
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTION: Obtain a working food thermometer for the establishment. A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.
